A resumed run that lost keyToTaskId would re-create every story as a duplicate. The checkpoint keyToTaskId is currently the ONLY reliable resolution path for child tickets and must not be lost.

REMEDIATION - IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-02, repair-only, no tickets created, updated or deleted. scripts/taskview-sync-board.mjs now pages list_tasks for the TOP-LEVEL roster only, then calls get_task on every discovered id and walks the returned subtasks array recursively to arbitrary depth, indexing each descendant's marker from its own note. TASKVIEW API DEFECT 4: the subtasks array embedded in a parent get_task reports tags as an empty array even when tags are set. Task 47 appeared with no tags inside get_task(27) but a direct get_task(47) returned [5,18,7,21]. Never verify a child's tags from the parent payload; re-read the child.

DEFECT 3 is now MITIGATED in the resolver. It remains a real TaskView API limitation - list_tasks still cannot see child tasks - but the script no longer depends on that path for children.

DEFECT 4 is now guarded in code: fetchChildTags(client, childId) re-reads a child with get_task and is the only tag-reading path. Verified by inspection that .subtasks is referenced solely for traversal and that no code reads tags from a parent payload.

TASKVIEW API DEFECT 5 (BLOCKING for Phase 4/5, found 2026-08-02 during the Phase 3 gate): list_tasks showCompleted is an EXCLUSIVE filter, not an inclusive one. showCompleted:false returns ONLY incomplete top-level tasks (13 on goal 3); showCompleted:true returns ONLY complete top-level tasks (2 on goal 3). Neither call returns all 15 epics. The union of both is required. CONSEQUENCE: the repaired scripts/taskview-sync-board.mjs pages the top-level roster with showCompleted:true, so it would see only the 2 completed epics, call get_task on those 2 alone, and miss 13 epics and all 63 of their stories. Its marker index would be almost entirely empty and a resumed run would re-create nearly the whole board. The script MUST be repaired again - page both showCompleted values and merge - before Phase 4 or Phase 5 runs with --apply. STATUS: MITIGATED IN THE RESOLVER 2026-08-02. The script now pages the top-level roster TWICE - once with showCompleted:false and once with showCompleted:true - then unions and deduplicates by task id before any recursion. The underlying API behaviour is unchanged; the script simply no longer depends on a single call returning everything.

blocker.permissionEvidence: Permission id 42 is graph_can_manage ('User can manage graph (reorder, add, edit, delete nodes, edges)') and id 43 is graph_can_view. Role 5 on goal 3 IS granted both 42 and 43. The 403 therefore does not come from role 5 lacking the permission - it points at the acting MCP principal not being assigned that role on goal 3, or at the graph-edge and role-admin endpoints requiring an owner-level scope the MCP token does not carry.
blocker.nonMutation: VERIFIED: the live dependency graph was re-read after both failures and is unchanged at 88 edges, ids 17-104, identical to the preflight baseline. Neither 403 performed a partial write. No task, tag, note, status or mapping was touched. No delete was attempted.
blocker.ownerActionNeeded: This is a human gate: granting a permission or role is an owner action. Confirm the MCP principal holds a role carrying graph_can_manage (permission 42) on goalId 3, then re-run Phase 5. All 16 edges are precomputed above and the run is fully resumable with zero rework.

incident.severity: recovered, no data loss, no duplicate
incident.what: A sed edit intended to correct a cosmetic '/10' progress label in the creation script introduced double quotes inside an already double-quoted f-string, producing a SyntaxError. The GitHub issue for AF-S0502 was created as #22, then the checkpoint step in the same script aborted before writing.
incident.impact: Issue #22 existed on GitHub for one turn without a checkpoint entry. Nothing else was affected; the failure was fail-closed - the checkpoint write simply did not happen rather than writing something wrong.
incident.recovery: The script was repaired, #22's URL was re-read from GitHub with gh issue view and written to the checkpoint before any further work. A marker query then confirmed EXACTLY ONE issue carries <!-- taskview-spec-key: AF-S0502 -->, so no duplicate was created.
incident.lesson: Never rewrite a quoted f-string with sed. The checkpoint-immediately discipline is what bounded the blast radius to a single recoverable entry.

subtaskConvention.issueBody: A subtask issue additionally carries a '**Parent story:**' line naming the parent spec key, parent TaskView id, parent deep link and parent issue URL, plus two extra markers: <!-- taskview-parent-key: KEY --> and <!-- taskview-parent-task-id: N -->.
subtaskConvention.noteSource: Subtasks sit at depth 2 and are INVISIBLE to list_tasks (the one-level nesting limit found in Phase 4/5), so a subtask's current note must be fetched with get_task rather than from the board sweep.
subtaskConvention.parentUntouched: Writing a subtask's GitHub line must not touch the parent. Proven for #43: its note is byte-identical before and after this batch, its Phase 4 child-index table and both child deep links are intact, and it still points at its own issue #4.
